items.title: North Korea declares it is not bound by nuclear treaty

featured_image.name: North Korean ambassador has stern words for US

items.description:
North Korea's top United Nations diplomat declared on Thursday that Pyongyang is not bound by the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty under any circumstances, reinforcing the country's insistence on being recognized as a nuclear weapons state during a major international conference in New York.

Ambassador Kim Song, North Korea's permanent representative to the UN, made the statement at the 11th NPT Review Conference, which is taking place at UN headquarters from April 27 to May 22. Kim criticized the United States and other Western nations for what he described as attempts to degrade the conference's atmosphere by raising the issue of North Korea's nuclear arsenal, according to state media outlet KCNA.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: U.S. jet disables Iranian tanker defying naval blockade

featured_image.name: Navy F/A-18 that got first air-to-air kill in years now fighting Iran

items.description:
A U.S. Navy F/A-18 Super Hornet fired 20mm cannon rounds into the rudder of an Iranian-flagged oil tanker on Wednesday, disabling the vessel as it attempted to reach an Iranian port in defiance of the American naval blockade, U.S. Central Command confirmed.

The incident, which occurred at 9 a.m. ET on May 6, marks the second time U.S. forces have used direct fire to stop a vessel from breaching the blockade since it began on April 13.

items.title: Iran's Ghalibaf vows nation 'will not surrender' amid US naval blockade

featured_image.name: Iran Parliament speaker Ghalibaf rises as key figure in US push to end war

items.description:
Iran's Parliament Speaker and top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf issued an audio message to the Iranian public on Wednesday accusing Washington of deploying a naval blockade, sanctions, and media manipulation to force Tehran into capitulation, as the country's economy buckles under the weight of a three-week-old maritime siege.

"The enemy is trying to dismantle internal cohesion through economic pressure and psychological warfare," Ghalibaf said, according to remarks carried by Iran's Fars news agency. He described the current moment as one of the most critical periods in Iran's modern history and said Washington was acting on "false intelligence" that would ultimately "cause everyone to suffer".[1]

items.title: Trump says Iran must send enriched uranium to US in deal

featured_image.name: Trump says Iran has agreed to hand over enriched uranium

items.description: President Donald Trump confirmed Wednesday that Iran's enriched uranium would be transferred to the United States as part of an emerging agreement to end the war, saying "No, not perhaps. It goes to the United States" when asked in a PBS News interview about the possibility of Tehran exporting its highly enriched nuclear material.[1][2]

items.title: US, Iran near 14-point memo to end Gulf war, awaiting Tehran's response

featured_image.name: Pakistani source said to confirm US, Iran closing in on memo to end war |  The Times of Israel

items.description: Iran confirmed on Wednesday that it is evaluating a new 14-point US proposal aimed at ending the more than two-month-long Gulf conflict, even as President Donald Trump warned that military action could resume at a higher intensity if Tehran rejects the terms.

items.title: Shipping industry balks at Hormuz transit despite IRGC safe-passage pledge

featured_image.name: IRGC promises safe passage via Strait of Hormuz after “ ...

items.description: Shipping companies are holding firm against resuming normal transits through the Strait of Hormuz, even as Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced "new protocols" for safe passage and signs of a potential U.S.-Iran peace agreement emerge following President Trump's pause of military operations in the waterway.

items.title: Ted Turner, CNN founder and media mogul, dies at 87

featured_image.name: Ted Turner, CNN founder and media mogul, dies at 87

items.description: Ted Turner, the brash media entrepreneur who launched the world's first 24-hour cable news network and reshaped how Americans consumed television, died Wednesday at age 87, according to Turner Enterprises. Turner died at his home near Tallahassee, Florida.[1][2]

items.title: Ted Turner, CNN founder and media mogul, dies at 87

featured_image.name: UN Foundation Pays Tribute to Founder and Chair Ted ...

items.description: Ted Turner, the maverick media mogul who founded CNN and transformed the landscape of American television, died Wednesday at age 87, according to Turner Enterprises. Turner, who had been living with Lewy body dementia since 2018, died at his home near Tallahassee, Florida.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Ukraine says Russia violated ceasefire with overnight strikes

featured_image.name: Ukraine Willing to Begin Talks if Russia Accepts 60 or 90-Day Ceasefire,  Says Sybiha — UNITED24 Media

items.description: Ukraine accused Russia on Wednesday of breaching the unilateral ceasefire declared by President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, with Russian forces launching 108 drones and three missiles at Ukrainian territory in the hours after the truce took effect at midnight on the night of May 5-6.

items.title: North Korea drops reunification from constitution, codifies Kim's nuclear authority

featured_image.name: North Korea removes reunification from its constitution

items.description:
North Korea has revised its constitution to remove all references to reunification with South Korea, formally codifying leader Kim Jong Un's doctrine of treating the two Koreas as hostile, separate states, according to a draft of the amended text reviewed by Reuters.[1][2]

The revision, believed to have been adopted during a March session of the Supreme People's Assembly, marks the first time North Korea has included a territorial clause in its constitution, Seoul National University professor Lee Jung-chul said at a South Korean Unification Ministry briefing on Wednesday.[3][4]

items.title: French container ship hit by missile in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: CMA CGM Vessel Navigates Hormuz as Crisis Remains 'Localized'

items.description:
French shipping giant CMA CGM confirmed on Wednesday that its Maltese-flagged container vessel, the CMA CGM San Antonio, was struck during an attack while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, injuring several crew members and damaging the ship.[1][2]

U.S. officials told CBS News the vessel was hit by what they described as a possible land-attack cruise missile late Tuesday evening local time, with several Filipino crew members among the injured. The wounded were evacuated and are receiving medical treatment, the company said in a statement to AFP.[3][4][1]

items.title: China's Big Fund in talks to lead DeepSeek round at $45B valuation

featured_image.name: China's DeepSeek is raising funds at $10 billion valuation ...

items.description:
China's largest state-backed semiconductor investment vehicle is in advanced negotiations to lead the first external funding round for AI startup DeepSeek at a valuation of approximately $45 billion, the Financial Times reported on Tuesday, citing four people familiar with the discussions.[1][2]

The China Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund — known in the industry as the "Big Fund" — would mark a dramatic expansion of its mandate, which has historically focused on chip fabrication, memory producers, and semiconductor equipment rather than AI model labs.[3][1]

items.title: Trump pauses Iran strikes, warns of escalation if no deal

featured_image.name: Trump extends pause on strikes against Iran's energy infrastructure

items.description: Iran confirmed on Wednesday that it is formally evaluating a US peace proposal as the two sides inch toward what a Pakistani mediator has described as a potential agreement to end the nearly 10-week war. President Donald Trump announced a temporary pause of "Project Freedom," the US military operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, citing "great progress" toward a deal — but warned that bombing would resume "at a much higher level and intensity" if Tehran refuses to come to terms.[1][2][3]

items.title: Spain to repatriate all passengers from hantavirus cruise ship

featured_image.name: M/V Hondius - Reef and Rainforest Tours

items.description: All passengers and crew remaining aboard the MV Hondius, a luxury expedition cruise ship struck by a deadly hantavirus outbreak, are currently asymptomatic, Spanish Health Minister Mónica García announced on Wednesday. The ship, which has been anchored near Cape Verde after being denied permission to dock, will now proceed to the Port of Granadilla in southern Tenerife, where passengers will be repatriated to their home countries.[1]

items.title: Trump pauses Hormuz escort operation, citing Iran deal progress

featured_image.name: Trump Says US to Pause Guiding Ships While Seeking Iran Deal - Bloomberg

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Tuesday that he is temporarily pausing "Project Freedom," the U.S. military operation to escort commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz, just one day after it launched. Trump cited "great progress" toward a deal with Iran and requests from mediator Pakistan and other countries, even as the naval blockade on Iranian ports remains fully in force.[1]

The pause came after a turbulent 24 hours in which the operation's launch on Monday triggered Iranian warning shots, attacks on commercial vessels, and strikes on Gulf states — escalating tensions that threatened to unravel the fragile ceasefire in place since April 7.[2][3]

items.title: US fires Tomahawk from Typhon launcher in Philippines for the first time

featured_image.name: US Army fires Tomahawk missile from new Typhon launcher during Philippines  drill

items.description:
The U.S. Army fired a Tomahawk cruise missile from its Typhon mid-range capability system on Philippine soil for the first time early Tuesday, launching from Tacloban City Airport on Leyte Island and striking a target roughly 600 kilometers (about 370 miles) away at Fort Magsaysay in Laur, Nueva Ecija, on the island of Luzon.[1][2][3]

The test came as China responded with a show of force over the disputed South China Sea, deploying H-6 bombers and J-16 fighter jets over Scarborough Shoal in what Beijing called "combat readiness" patrols.[4][5]

items.title: Cargo vessel hit in Strait of Hormuz amid US 'Project Freedom' launch

featured_image.name: Cargo vessel struck by projectile at Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says | Reuters

items.description: A cargo vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to a report from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency, Reuters reported. The attack marks the latest in a string of maritime incidents in one of the world's most critical shipping lanes, as the United States pursues a new military initiative to reopen the waterway.[1]

items.title: Rubio calls Israel-Lebanon peace 'imminently achievable'

featured_image.name: Rubio says Israel-Lebanon peace deal is achievable but Hezbollah is a  problem | Reuters

items.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio declared Tuesday that a peace deal between Israel and Lebanon is "imminently achievable," while identifying Hezbollah as the central obstacle to any lasting agreement between the two nations.

"By and large, I think a peace deal between Lebanon and Israel is imminently achievable, and should be," Rubio told reporters at a White House press briefing. "The problem with Israel and Lebanon is not Israel or Lebanon, it's Hezbollah."[1][2]

items.title: Rubio says Taiwan will come up at Trump-Xi summit next week

featured_image.name: Tough talk on Taiwan - GZERO Media

items.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed on Tuesday that Taiwan will be a topic of discussion when President Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14-15, warning against any "destabilizing" actions regarding the self-governing island as the high-stakes summit approaches.

"I'm sure Taiwan will be a topic of conversation; it always is," Rubio said during a White House press briefing, adding that neither Washington nor Beijing has an interest in seeing instability in the Indo-Pacific region.[1][2][3]

items.title: Pentagon says Iran ceasefire 'still intact' despite clashes in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Trump refuses to say if US-Iran ceasefire holds after shots ...

items.description: President Donald Trump warned on Monday that Iran would be "blown off the face of the Earth" if its forces targeted American vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, as the fragile ceasefire between the two nations appeared to buckle under escalating military clashes tied to the U.S.-led naval escort operation known as Project Freedom.
